plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden flower heads that follow the sun across the sky. Each head is a crowd of tiny florets, ringed by bright yellow petal-like rays. In early August, fields across the plains glow in warm shades of yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Great Plains of North America and sunflower fields across the temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower. It is hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers packed into a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of fragrant purple blooms that hum with bees. Its soothing scent drifts across gardens and the hillside fields of Provence, where the harvest is in full swing in late July and early August.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe, especially Provence in southern France, and gardens across the temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Lavender's name comes from the Latin word for washing, because the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem bursts into fluffy golden pom-poms that cover the whole tree in late winter. Its honey-sweet scent fills the bush as the southern winter begins to turn toward spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (July to October in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, New South Wales and South Australia
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the golden wattle has been the country's official floral emblem since 1988.
